title: Chapter 21: Reflection, Annotations, Modules, and Metaprogramming
description: Understand and contain the runtime mechanisms used by frameworks. Learners inspect Class metadata, invoke members with validated types, design annotation retention and processing, explain method handles and bridge methods, diagnose class-loader identity and leaks, and declare JPMS exports, opens, services, and runtime images without weakening boundaries casually.

lessons.title: Class objects and reflective type inspection
lessons.theoryMarkdown:
# Class objects and reflective type inspection

## Runtime metadata
Class<?> describes a runtime type whose precise generic identity is unknown to the caller.
```java
Class<?> type = String.class;
System.out.println(type.getName()); // java.lang.String
for (var method : type.getDeclaredMethods()) {
    System.out.println(method.getName());
}
```
T.class, object.getClass(), and Class.forName obtain Class objects in different ways. getMethods includes inherited public methods; getDeclaredMethods reports members declared on that type, including nonpublic ones. Enumeration order is not a stable report contract.

## Scope the mechanism
Reflection is useful for serializers, dependency wiring, and tooling. Ordinary domain code is usually clearer with explicit interfaces. Generic signature metadata may be available, but runtime object checks still cannot generally prove List<String> from its erased class.

## Practice
Inspect a record's components and a class's public constructors. Sort metadata before printing a deterministic report. Compare getMethods and getDeclaredMethods on a subclass. Reject arbitrary class names from untrusted requests; an inspection tool should define an allowlist and access policy.

lessons.title: Constructors, fields, methods, method handles, and access control
lessons.theoryMarkdown:
# Constructors, fields, methods, method handles, and access control

## Lookup and invocation fail at runtime
```java
var method = String.class.getMethod("substring", int.class);
Object result = method.invoke("Java", 1);
System.out.println(result); // ava
```
This fragment requires handling reflective checked exceptions. Method lookup uses exact parameter types, so int.class differs from Integer.class. Invocation can fail because the receiver, arguments, accessibility, or called method is wrong. InvocationTargetException wraps a failure thrown by the target; inspect its cause.

## Access boundaries
setAccessible is not universal permission to bypass modules. Strong encapsulation can reject deep access. Opening a package for reflection is a deployment/API decision, not a routine fix for every diagnostic.

MethodHandle represents a typed executable reference with lookup-based access checking. It can support dynamic runtime machinery, but its invocation typing and adaptation rules require care.

## Beyond invoking existing members
Testing and mocking frameworks such as Mockito usually do not rely on reflective invocation alone to fabricate a mock. They use bytecode-generation libraries (ByteBuddy, or the older cglib and ASM) to synthesize a new proxy subclass at runtime, override its methods, and define that generated class into the JVM. The mock then behaves like ordinary compiled code rather than paying reflective dispatch overhead on every call.

## Practice
Invoke a valid method, request a nonexistent signature, and invoke a method that throws. Report these as different failures. Compare reflective invocation with an interface call and justify why reflection is necessary before using it in application logic.

lessons.title: Class loaders, delegation, plugins, identity, and loader leaks
lessons.theoryMarkdown:
# Class loaders, delegation, plugins, identity, and loader leaks

## A name alone is not runtime identity
The defining class loader and binary name together identify a runtime class. Two loaders can define classes with identical names and bytes that are not assignment-compatible. This matters for plugins and redeployed applications.

```java
System.out.println(String.class.getClassLoader()); // bootstrap represented as null
System.out.println(Main.class.getClassLoader());
```
The bootstrap loader supplies foundational classes. Other loaders commonly delegate to parents before defining their own classes, though custom policies exist. Class loading, linking, and initialization are related stages; initialization can trigger static code.

## Retention
A long-lived thread, listener, cache, or ThreadLocal referencing a plugin object can retain its defining loader and associated classes after apparent unloading. Clearing one application field is insufficient if another route remains.

## Practice
Inspect loaders for platform and application classes. Sketch two plugins sharing an API loader but owning implementation loaders. Explain why placing duplicate API classes in both child loaders breaks interoperability. Design explicit plugin shutdown that unregisters listeners and closes resources before releasing loader references.

exercises.title: Class loaders, delegation, plugins, identity, and loader leaks: concept check
choices: Binary name plus defining class loader
hints: Think about why two plugins that each define a class with the same name and bytes can still fail an instanceof check against one another.

lessons.title: JPMS descriptors, requires, exports, opens, services, and jlink
lessons.theoryMarkdown:
# JPMS descriptors, requires, exports, opens, services, and jlink

## Modules declare reliable boundaries
```java
module academy.app {
    requires java.net.http;
    exports academy.api;
}
```
This belongs in module-info.java. requires expresses module dependencies; exports makes public types in a package available to other modules. opens permits reflective access and can be restricted to selected modules. Exporting a package does not automatically open private internals.

## Services and runtime images
uses declares consumption of a service interface; provides ... with ... declares providers. ServiceLoader discovers implementations without application code constructing each provider directly. jlink creates a runtime image from a resolved module graph; it is not a general replacement for packaging arbitrary nonmodular dependencies.

Classpath code belongs to unnamed modules and differs from explicit module-path code. Split packages and automatic modules complicate migration; inspect the actual dependency graph.

## Practice
Create a tiny API module and implementation module, compile them on a module path, and attempt access to an unexported package. Add a ServiceLoader provider. Explain whether a serializer truly requires opens and limit it to the relevant package and module.

lessons.title: Chapter 21 assessment and deliberate practice
lessons.theoryMarkdown:
# Chapter 21 assessment

Bring together Class metadata inspection, reflective invocation, annotation retention, class-loader identity, and JPMS boundaries to solve the decision scenario and repair **Reflective primitive parameter type**, where a lookup written against the wrong parameter type must be corrected without hiding the mismatch behind a hard-coded result. Write a prediction before running the debugger and preserve the intended reflective operation when fixing it.

The function exercise is a bounded practice task, not proof of every chapter competency. Complete the implementation and external practice described in the five lessons as well. Review the changed source for its contract, then explain the relevant tradeoff without consulting the answer.

exercises.title: Inspect a record's runtime components
exercises.instructionMarkdown: Implement componentNames(String selector). Use Class.getRecordComponents to report component names in declaration order for the provided nested Task and Owner records. selector Task -> id,title; Owner -> name; any other text -> empty string. Keep the nested records and inspect their metadata rather than hard-coding the outputs. Tests verify results; source review checks actual reflection.
hints: Call getRecordComponents() on the Class object for the matched record and read each component's name in declaration order, rather than hard-coding the two known selectors.
Make sure an unmatched or case-mismatched selector (such as lowercase "task") falls through to the empty-string result instead of throwing or matching accidentally.

exercises.title: Reflective primitive parameter type
exercises.instructionMarkdown: The supplied program looks up `substring` with `Integer.class` as the parameter type, but `String.substring` is declared with the primitive `int` parameter, so the reflective lookup fails before it can run. Repair the lookup so it matches the declared signature and the program writes exactly `ava`. Preserve the reflective invocation and explain why the parameter type mismatch changes the result; do not replace it with a hard-coded print. Output tests verify the result; preserving the intended reflective operation requires source review.
hints: The declared parameter is primitive int; reflective lookup requires that Class.
